name: Necessary residual-dimension obstruction for null-projected SYM under N1-N5
target: Phys. Rev. D 99 (2019) 046004, Sec. III A: the existence proofs of Nishino (Nucl. Phys. B 523 (1998) 450) for super Yang-Mills theories in (9+m)+(1+m) can be successfully repeated in (9+8n)+1, (10+8n)+2, (11+8n)+3 and (12+8n)+4, including 27+3 and 19+3
result: False for n >= 1: a super Yang-Mills theory with a Majorana-Weyl gaugino built on k null vectors in Nishino's manner (axioms N1-N5, which his construction satisfies) has k <= min(s,t) and residual dimension s+t-2k in {2, 10}, because the cubic gaugino terms reduce to a Fierz identity that holds only when the spinors have dimension 2(d-2), that is d in {3, 4, 6, 10}; so s-t lies in {8, 0, -8}, and none of the four families with n >= 1, nor 27+3 or 19+3, carries such a theory. For one time, in (9+8n)+1 with n >= 1, every massless multiplet of a unitary theory without tensor charges has at least 2^(2^(2+4n)) states, so there is no massless vector multiplet. For the same unitary, tensor-charge-free single-time class with finite helicity spectrum, a written helicity argument gives span at least S/8; scalar, spinor and vector polarizations have span at most two, so arbitrary finite multiplicities of those fields require S <= 16.

notes.proof: Written converse for the cubic identity; null-frame and Witt reduction under N1-N5. The 24 October 2026 revision makes graded translation symmetry explicit, proves the null-current wedge statement, and adds the helicity argument needed to exclude arbitrary finite low-spin multiplicities. These are necessary conditions, not existence constructions for all remaining signatures.
notes.formal: No full Lean formalisation of these field-theoretic statements; gamma-matrix numerical checks do not discharge this gate.
notes.code: construct/multitime_sym.py rebuilds the Witt bound, the dimension count and the single-time bound, with two refuters (the mod-8 rule of the claim, complex null frames)
